initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the file can show the share of reported Brooklyn crash events with a pedestrian casualty, but not pedestrian exposure or risk per trip, and crash reporting does not cover every road event.
initial_plan.metric: Annual percentage of Brooklyn crash reports with one or more pedestrians injured or killed.
initial_plan.denominator: All police-reported crash rows with borough Brooklyn in that calendar year; numerator is rows in that denominator with number_of_pedestrians_injured + number_of_pedestrians_killed greater than zero.
initial_plan.population: Police-reported crash events in Brooklyn, counting one row per crash; only crashes with known Brooklyn borough are included.
filters: crash year is 2013 or later through the latest year present
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest year present in the file, inclusive; assess whether the first or last year is only partially covered.

facts.year_coverage: 2013-2025 have observations from January 1 through December 31; 2026 is partial, January 1 through June 11.
facts.rows: Across 2013-2025 there are 2,132,218 crash rows, of which 473,801 have borough Brooklyn; in partial 2026, 36,424 rows total and 9,700 Brooklyn rows.
facts.borough_quality: 659,713 of 2,132,218 rows (30.9%) in 2013-2025 have a missing, blank, unknown, or nonstandard borough label under the check's five-official-borough validation; 668,406 of 2,168,642 do over 2013-2026.
facts.outcome_quality: Among Brooklyn rows in 2013-2026, 0 have number_of_pedestrians_injured missing and 0 have number_of_pedestrians_killed missing; 0 rows have either missing.
facts.date_quality: 0 Brooklyn rows have a missing grouping date; 0 rows in the planned date window have a missing date.

decisions.borough: Exclude rows with missing, blank, unknown, or nonstandard borough labels because their Brooklyn location cannot be established; 659,713 rows (30.9%) of all crash rows in final years are thereby outside the identifiable borough population. Retain only Brooklyn rows; other valid boroughs are outside scope.
decisions.outcomes: Keep all qualifying Brooklyn rows because neither pedestrian outcome field is missing; no rows are dropped for outcome missingness.
decisions.years: Exclude 2026 because it ends on June 11 and is only partly covered; retain complete years 2013-2025.
decisions.grouping_date: Keep all qualifying rows; no Brooklyn grouping dates are missing.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: this measures the share of reported Brooklyn crash events involving a pedestrian casualty, not pedestrian exposure or risk per trip/person, so it cannot establish whether the road network became safer for an individual pedestrian.
final_plan.metric: Annual percentage of eligible Brooklyn crash reports with one or more pedestrians injured or killed; numerator counts reports with number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0 or number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0.
final_plan.denominator: All police-reported Brooklyn crash rows in that calendar year with both pedestrian outcome fields nonmissing; these fields are complete for every included Brooklyn row, so this is all Brooklyn crash rows.
final_plan.population: Police-reported crash events (one row per crash) with borough Brooklyn; reports with unidentifiable borough are excluded.
filters: both pedestrian outcome fields are nonmissing
final_plan.years: Complete calendar years 2013-2025; exclude partial 2026 (data through June 11).
final_plan.limitations: This is the share of police-reported Brooklyn crash rows involving a pedestrian casualty, not a per-trip or per-person risk; it can change as the mix and count of reported crashes change. 659,713 of 2,132,218 crash rows (30.9%) in 2013-2025 have missing, blank, unknown, or nonstandard borough labels and are excluded because their borough cannot be identified. There are no missing pedestrian outcome fields in Brooklyn rows; the partial 2026 year is excluded.
